A_target.statement:
Let $p$ and $q$ be [[Definition:Probability Distribution|probability distributions]] on a finite set with all $q_i > 0$.
Then:
:$\displaystyle \map D {p \parallel q} = \sum_i p_i \log \frac {p_i} {q_i} \ge 0$
with equality {{iff}} $p = q$.

B_source.statement:
Let $\phi$ be [[Definition:Strictly Convex Real Function|strictly convex]] and $X$ an integrable random variable.
Then $\expect {\map \phi X} \ge \map \phi {\expect X}$, with equality {{iff}} $X$ is almost surely constant.

substitutions.the random variable X: q_i / p_i, taken with probability p_i

object_map.reformulation: Write relative entropy as the expectation of -log of a likelihood ratio and apply Jensen.

validity_conditions: Terms with p_i = 0 contribute 0 and are omitted, so the sum of q over the support may be less than 1.
Strict convexity of -log gives the equality case.
proof_plan:
Let $X = \dfrac {q_i} {p_i}$ with probability $p_i$, for $i$ in the support of $p$.
Then $\map D {p \parallel q} = \expect {-\log X}$.

By the source result, as $-\log$ is strictly convex:
:$\expect {-\log X} \ge -\log \expect X = -\log \displaystyle \sum_{p_i \mathop > 0} q_i \ge -\log 1 = 0$
Equality forces $X$ to be constant, say $q_i = c p_i$ on the support, and $\displaystyle \sum_{p_i > 0} q_i = 1$, so $c = 1$ and $q$ vanishes off the support.

Hence equality holds {{iff}} $p = q$, which is [[Gibbs' Inequality]].
{{qed}}
